summary: The note describes Lake Manzala, a brackish lake sometimes called a lagoon in northeastern Egypt on the Nile Delta. It lies near Port Said and a few miles from the ancient ruins at Tanis. It is the largest of Egypt's northern deltaic lakes, and its size is given as of 2008.
one_line: Lake Manzala is a large brackish lagoon-like lake on the Nile Delta in northeastern Egypt, near Port Said.
key_facts: Lake Manzala is also known as Manzaleh.
Lake Manzala is a brackish lake, sometimes called a lagoon.
Lake Manzala is located in northeastern Egypt on the Nile Delta.
Lake Manzala lies near Port Said.
Lake Manzala is a few miles from the ancient ruins at Tanis.
Lake Manzala is the largest of the northern deltaic lakes of Egypt.
As of 2008, Lake Manzala is 47 km long.
As of 2008, Lake Manzala is 30 km wide.
The Arabic name of Lake Manzala is given as "baḥīrat manzala".
